title: Strict integral finite-coefficient pullback tower
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$ and its fixed uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site of $W$ use the completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq0}S_{W,n}$, with $S_{W,n}=(A/\varpi^{n+1})_W$ and its specified limit projections [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For every unbounded cochain complex $P$ of $R_Y$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $P_n=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_{Y,n}$ with its actual quotient transition $r_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Use the ordinary finite module pullback $g_n^*$ and its adjunction-unit generators $\eta_n$ [def-pur-integral-finite-pullback]. Define $\operatorname{Res}_n$ termwise by restriction along $R_X\to S_{X,n}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and define $B_g^0(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*(P_n)$. Its transition $\tau_n$ is the canonical natural chain map, linear over $R_X$, characterized in every degree and on every base-changed site object by $\tau_n(\eta_{n+1}(x))=\eta_n(r_n(x))$. In tensor notation it sends $g^{-1}(x)\otimes a$ to $g^{-1}(r_n)(g^{-1}(x))\otimes\rho_n(a)$, where $\rho_n:S_{X,n+1}\to S_{X,n}$ is coefficient reduction. Define $B_g^0$ on chain maps by finite reduction, finite pullback and restriction in every level, retaining these transitions. Thus $B_g^0$ is a functor from cochain complexes of $R_Y$-modules to strict inverse sequences of cochain complexes of $R_X$-modules. There is no flatness, K-flatness, boundedness, constructibility or invertibility hypothesis; the coefficient and scheme universes are independent.
